name: ANSI/IEEE shielded conductor symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented shielded conductor drawn with a dashed or broken outline around the wire to show a shield.
description: In IEEE-oriented drawings a shielded conductor is commonly shown with a broken or dashed enclosure around the conductor, sometimes with a short lead to a ground symbol. US instrumentation drawings use it for analogue signal wiring, thermocouple extension leads and drive feedback.

This is an independently drawn explanation of the convention, not a reproduction of the IEEE graphic. As with the IEC form, the outline does not say where the shield is grounded, which must be shown at the shield lead. Shield drain wires should have their own terminal numbers.
readingNotes: Check whether the shield is grounded at one end only.
drawingChecklist: Assign terminal numbers to drain wires.
Record shield type in the cable schedule.
distinction: A shielded conductor intercepts interference; a coaxial cable uses its outer conductor as the signal return.
